name: Mavis Shumate
languages: The old ballads her grandmother sang, every verse, which is a language of its own on the ridge
equipment: Heavy coat: her father's mackinaw, red and black plaid, cut down to fit her and still too long
Lever-action rifle, her father's .30-30 carbine, a deer rifle she has carried since she was fourteen
Hatchet, a good one, for kindling, blazes and the occasional copperhead
A sang hoe and a canvas bag for ginseng, which she digs in September and sells to a buyer in Gale for more than the company store would ever give
A coal-oil lantern, a pint of kerosene, matches in a twist of oilcloth
Her grandfather's 1898 deed, which sold the coal under Shumate Ridge to the Ottway company for fifty cents an acre and kept the surface, with a clause in it nobody in the family can quite read
A plug of tobacco for trading, a pocket knife, and a heel of cornbread in wax paper
features: Up Before Dawn (Farm-Raised origin: needs only 6 hours for a long rest; can't be surprised while awake in the last hour before sunrise; advantage on saves against exhaustion from hard work, cold and lost sleep; notices without a check when animals are frightened or behaving wrongly)

Know Your Quarry (Hunter: after an hour studying a creature's sign, she declares it her quarry; advantage on Survival to track it and Perception to find it, she always knows which way it went from a place where she found its sign, and once on each of her turns a weapon hit on it deals an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type)

Fieldcraft (Hunter: she can't become lost in woods or hill country except by something not natural, moves at normal pace while moving stealthily outdoors, and in a short rest sets a snare or tripwire bell that warns her of anything within 30 ft of camp)

Cold Focus (Hunter, 2nd level: when she fails a fear check against her quarry she still gains the Dread but has advantage on her next attack against it; when she succeeds, she can move half her speed without provoking opportunity attacks)
Way of the Hunt: Hunter of the Uncanny (Hunter, 3rd level: once she has declared a supernatural creature her quarry, the GM tells her one of its rules about what hurts it or bars it)

Hired On (Farmhand background: at any farm in the county she can get a meal and a place in the barn for a day's work, farm people talk to her as an equal, and she notices without a check when a farm's rhythm is wrong)

personality.traits: I say what I think and then I think about it. I'd rather be in the woods than in any room with more than three people in it. I can tell you where every spring, every rock house and every sang patch on this ridge is, and I won't.
personality.ideals: The land is the land. The company bought what's under it for fifty cents an acre from an old man who couldn't read the paper, and they think that means they own the whole mountain. They don't own the top.
personality.bonds: My mother, Verlie, sixty-six, and the farm: forty acres of steep pasture, an orchard and a spring. Lettie Burchett, who caught me. My daddy, Cletus, who went up to the old air shaft in October 1919 because he heard the men knocking, and got run off by company guards with a gun in his back, and never got over it.
personality.flaws: I'm proud and I'm short with people, especially company people and especially town people who think I'm simple because I talk slow. I've seen a light walking in our upper pasture since March, over the old shaft, and I haven't told Mama because I can't think how.

appearance: A tall, rawboned woman of thirty-four with a sun-browned face, high cheekbones, a long brown braid going grey at the front, and level hazel eyes that take their time. A red and black plaid mackinaw, a man's felt hat, overalls, boots, a rifle on a sling and a hatchet in her belt; she walks the ridge in a straight line no matter what is in the way.
backstory: Mavis Shumate's great-grandfather cleared the top of the ridge above Kettle Run in the 1840s, and the family has farmed it since, cattle and corn and apples, with a little country coal bank dug into the hillside for the house. In 1898 her grandfather sold the coal rights under the whole ridge to the Ottway Smokeless Coal Company for fifty cents an acre, on a deed that lets the company do nearly anything below ground and a good deal above it, and in 1909 the company sank its Number Two air shaft in the Shumates' upper pasture, two hundred feet down to the north workings, and built a fence round it. The shaft was abandoned and timbered over in 1916. In October 1919, when 7 North blew, her father Cletus went up to the old shaft at night and put his ear to the timbers and heard men knocking, far below, and saw daylight's grey come and go in the cracks; on the morning of the 17th company men came up the ridge road with a truck, a mixer and two guards, and when he tried to tell them, the guards walked him back to the house with a rifle in his back. They poured two feet of concrete over the shaft that day. Cletus died in 1924, and Mavis has worked the farm with her mother since. She has hunted every inch of the ridge, she knows the old country bank her grandfather dug and the place inside it where, in 1916, the company's miners broke through from below and then bricked the hole up again. Since March she has seen a pale light in the upper pasture at night, moving over the concrete cap, and found the grass around the cap white with frost on April mornings. She came down to the camp to see Lettie about it, and walked into the middle of everything else.
